skill.name: set-up-shopware-google-ads-conversion-tracking
skill.description: Set up and troubleshoot server-side conversion tracking for a Shopware sales channel with Product Metrics and Google Ads. Check consent settings, secondary conversion actions, and paid test order delivery.
skill.summary: Connect Shopware to Google Ads and verify consent-aware purchase tracking.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown formatting, vendor links, or scoped setup steps rather than shell substitution or reconnaissance. Confirmed risks include live writes without explicit approval, broad order lookups, and unpinned installation. The workflow also needs clearer boundaries for remote instructions, credentials, consent, and features outside purchase tracking.

remediation.issue: Approval for live writes is not required.
remediation.suggestion: Before any write, confirm the workspace, sales channel, Google Ads client account, and proposed changes. Use idempotency only to control retries.

remediation.issue: Order lookups can expose more data than validation needs.
remediation.suggestion: Use a known test order ID and return only delivery status. Bound any search to the approved sales channel and avoid displaying raw order records.

remediation.issue: The installation example does not pin the package runner target or the skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Provide reviewed, immutable versions for the installer and skill. Require separate approval before executing the installer.

remediation.issue: Remote documentation and returned browser links lack explicit trust checks.
remediation.suggestion: Treat fetched pages as reference material, not instructions with tool authority. Verify destination hosts and requested permissions before handing a link to the operator.

remediation.issue: Linked setup guides include features outside base Shopware purchase tracking.
remediation.suggestion: Limit this workflow to Shopware and Google Ads purchase tracking. Require separate approval for additional channels, customer data terms, or Customer Match.

remediation.issue: The secrets rule lets the agent handle credentials for unrelated integrations.
remediation.suggestion: Remove those exceptions and direct users to enter credentials in the provider interface. Do not pass credentials as shell arguments.

remediation.issue: The first-party collector is presented as a way around browser blocking.
remediation.suggestion: Document what is collected and sent for each consent state. Test refusal and withdrawal, and require consent before collecting or forwarding advertising data.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Content Can Influence Setup Actions
semantic_findings.description: The workflow treats live vendor Markdown as equivalent to bundled instructions and asks users to open tool-returned URLs without explicit destination checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both handoffs are explicit. A changed page or an unexpected tool response can redirect the workflow, but no active injection appears in the reviewed files.

semantic_findings.title: Connection Guides Expand Data Sharing Scope
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends users to generic connection guides that include other ad destinations, Enhanced Conversions terms, and Customer Match. Those steps exceed base purchase tracking.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main file excludes these features, but the linked guides present some as setup steps. Following them broadly could grant access beyond the original request.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exceptions Extend Beyond Shopware and Google Ads
semantic_findings.description: The secrets rule allows the assistant to receive unrelated integration credentials and pass them to commands. It does not specify a protected input channel.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rule names three unrelated credential exceptions. The Shopware guide instead keeps its pairing token out of chat, and no credential exposure was observed.

semantic_findings.title: First-Party Tracking Reduces Browser Blocking
semantic_findings.description: The skill promotes server-side delivery and a generated first-party collector path to avoid browser blocking. This makes storefront consent checks especially important.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The design explicitly reduces browser blocking. The guides describe honoring banner consent and withdrawal, so the files do not establish a consent bypass.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopware Conversion Tracking for Google Ads
content.value_statement: Browser tags can miss eligible Shopware purchases, and setup or consent issues can make gaps hard to diagnose. Use Product Metrics to configure server-side reporting and verify a paid test order.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status and identify the next incomplete step.
Guide the operator through pairing one Shopware sales channel with the Product Metrics plugin.
Guide Google Ads client account connection, Merchant Center linking, and Data Manager approval.
Match the consent configuration to the banner on the storefront.
Guide creation of eight secondary conversion actions and explain how costs affect profit reporting.
Check whether a paid test order arrived in Product Metrics.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a compatible Shopware 6.7 setup, and PHP 8.2 or later.
Each plugin installation tracks one sales channel, and only eligible paid orders are sent.
The operator completes Shopware and Google sign-ins, access grants, plugin pairing, and any changes to primary conversion actions.
This workflow does not configure Enhanced Conversions, Customer Match, or bidding.

use_cases.title: Set Up Purchase Measurement
use_cases.description: Connect a single storefront to the Google Ads client account and verify purchase tracking with a paid test order.

use_cases.title: Check a Conversion Count Gap
use_cases.description: Check payment status, channel pairing, and consent before treating a mismatch as a tracking failure.

use_cases.title: Validate a Server-Side Rollout
use_cases.description: Check plugin pairing and order sync while the existing Google Ads purchase action remains primary.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: List the accounts, permissions, and Shopware versions I need for server-side Google Ads purchase tracking. Do not change any settings.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Next Setup Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the Product Metrics setup status for [workspace] and [sales channel]. List the missing steps and ask before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Paid Test Order
prompt_templates.prompt: Check delivery for test order [order ID] in [sales channel]. Report only delivery status and the next diagnostic check.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Tracking Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [sales channel] and [Google Ads client account] before migration. Check consent, Data Manager access, and secondary actions without changing bidding or duplicating conversions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Specialist reviewing measurement before a production change

output_examples.input: Which setup step is missing after I connect the Shopware plugin?
output: Google Ads still needs Data Manager access.
Grant access in Google, then check the storefront consent setting before creating secondary actions.

output_examples.input: Why did my paid test order not appear in conversion reporting?
output: The test order has not appeared in Product Metrics yet.
Confirm it was paid in the paired sales channel and allow a few minutes for sync.
Then check that Product Metrics uses the banner shown on that storefront.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, paired storefront, Google Ads client account, and proposed changes before authorizing writes.
Keep the pairing token in the Shopware plugin settings and out of chat.
Test consent and delivery with a known test order before changing any primary conversion action.
anti_patterns: Connect a Google Ads manager account instead of the client account that runs the campaigns.
Select a consent provider that the storefront does not display.
Make the existing purchase action and a new purchase action primary at the same time.

faq.question: Does this work with Shopware 5?
faq.answer: No. The guide requires Shopware 6.7 with PHP 8.2 or later. It lists the plugin build for Shopware 6.7.14.0.

faq.question: Can I use Shopware's built-in cookie manager?
faq.answer: Yes. Leave the Product Metrics consent provider unconfigured to use Shopware's cookie manager.

faq.question: Is Merchant Center required?
faq.answer: Yes. Link Merchant Center to the Google Ads client account and connect it in Product Metrics.

faq.question: Can one installation cover several sales channels?
faq.answer: No. Each installation is paired with one Shopware sales channel.

faq.question: Do I need to remove my existing Google Ads tag?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics creates secondary actions alongside existing tracking. Review primary actions before switching to avoid counting the same purchase twice.

faq.question: What happens to refunds and cancellations?
faq.answer: Product Metrics uses Shopware refund and cancellation records to adjust the Google Ads conversion.
